notes.title: A brand new patch 1.1.2 is released!
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings Dieslpunk Builders![/h1]

We only recently left Early Access and published the incredible patch 1.1.0 (and the less impressive but still important patch 1.1.1). But we're not slowing down! We have a brand new patch for today which should greatly improve your experience. [b]Check out the changelog below:[/b]

[list]
[*] New buildings are added to the 'Fortification' tab in Battle Simulator, including new turrets, barriers, and structures to destroy.
[*] Turrets placed in Battle Simulator no longer sink into the ground.
[*] Enemy vehicles in Endless Mode won't spawn if there's an obstacle in the way.
[*] Fixed an issue that could cause the Endless Mode to (ironically) never end, even after defeat.
[*] Players are now given a bigger budget when constructing their first flying vehicle in the Campaign Mode.
[*] The base defense missions on the first map of the Campaign Mode are now easier and unlock more modules.
[*] Performance is now a bit better on the first four maps.
[*] Vehicles will no longer be impaired by small rocks or debris, making it a lot easier to traverse difficult terrain!
[/list]

These new changes should make it a lot easier for new players to start playing Dieselpunk Wars. We're also very excited by the recent additions to the Battle Simulator. You can see an example of what you can do with these new structures by[b] downloading our scenario[/b]:
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2497661488

You don't need to download any vehicles to check it out. Just subscribe to this scenario on the Steam Workshop, launch the game, start a Battle Simulator on the Valley map and have some fun storming an enemy position!

Did you prepare a scenario you wish to share with your friends? Then all you need to do is [b]post it via Steam Workshop![/b] You can do this by doing the following steps:
[olist]
[*] Once you're done creating a scenario in Battle Simulator, click on the Save/Load button near the top left corner of the screen.
[*] Name your scenario and press "Save".
[*] Click on the recently saved scenario so that it's highlighted with a green frame.
[*] Press the "Publish to Steam" button and wait for a few seconds while the scenario is being uploaded.
[*] Once your scenario is on the Steam Workshop, you will receive a notification. You can then add a description to your scenario using the Steam interface.
[/olist]

Thank you for your feedback over the last few days! Most of these recent improvements were made in response to our wonderful community and your valuable comments. We hope that with this new build you'll have even more fun playing Dieselpunk Wars!

With regards
[b]Image Power team[/b]

notes.title: Patch 1.1.1 is out! Check out the changelog!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/c79bb06b97636a60b3ae5d1f0799f28fd4eb4066.jpg[/img]

[h2]Hello Dieselpunk Builders![/h2]

As you have probably noticed, Dieselpunk Wars officially left Early Access on the 13th of May. We would like to thank everybody who joined us for the celebration during our release live stream. If you missed it, you can watch a VOD of the live stream here:
[previewyoutube=2MyuRhLfOvs;full][/previewyoutube]

When Dieselpunk Wars left Early Access, we also released the long-awaited patch 1.1.0. Soon after, we also launched a hotfix 1.1.1, addressing some issues with scenario sharing on Steam Workshop. We have been talking about these updates for weeks before the release but we never did share complete patch notes. This post is here to fix that!

[h2]Check out the changelog below:[/h2]

[list]
[*] Added new functionality that allows scenario sharing via Steam Workshop.
[*] Created a new tab "Fortifications" in Battle Simulator, which allows the players to add buildings to Battle Simulator.
[*] Reworked Battle Simulator UI to work with new functionalities.
[*] A vehicle can now be designated as a "Player Vehicle" in the Battle simulator.
[*] Vessels can now be marked as targets for the Player Vehicle.
[*] Added a button to copy a selected vehicle in Battle Simulator ('E' by default).
[*] It's now possible to plan move orders for AI-controlled vehicles in the Battle Simulator.
[/list]
[hr][/hr] 
[h3]Developer comment:[/h3]
[i]Simply put, all of the above features allow you to create your own missions in Battle Simulator and share them with your friends via Steam Workshop. Scenario sharing works similarly to vehicle sharing. When you start a scenario in which one of the vehicles is a "Player Vehicle", you will take control of the chosen vehicle instead of the usual battle simulation. Your task, as a player, will be to either destroy marked targets or defeat every vehicle on the opposing teams.

As a scenario creator, you can set up elaborate battle plans, position enemy vehicles behind heavy fortifications, and prepare patrol routes for the AI. And then order the player to destroy a heavily guarded convoy or break into a fortified facility. And as a player, all you have to do is download that scenario, open it in Battle Simulator, and have fun!

Just remember that if you share a scenario with custom-made vehicles, you need to publish those vehicles via Steam Workshop too. Otherwise, other players won't be able to use your scenario.[/i]
[hr][/hr] 
[h2]Now, for the rest of the changelog:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added a new map called "Valley", perfect for large-scale vehicles and for custom scenarios in Battle Simulator.
[*] New blocks were added, including new viewports and Detachable Joints, which you can use to split your vehicle into smaller pieces or merge a few vehicles into one larger vessel.
[*] Improved vehicle physics.
[*] It's now possible to modify physics settings, including gravity or air drag, in the Creative Mode.
[*] Rotors now have an additional function, which allows them to be controlled by a mouse (this can be enabled individually for each rotor in Build Mode).
[*] Translations have been improved, big thanks to our community for feedback and suggestions regarding these changes!
[*] And many, many bugfixes...
[/list]

We've discussed individual parts of this changelog in the days leading up to the patch's release. For more detailed information on any of them, please check out our previous Steam announcements. And if there is anything else that you want to ask us about, feel free to reach out to us in the comments or on our official Discord server.

We can't wait to see the scenarios you come up with!

With regards
[b]Image Power team[/b]

notes.title: Dieselpunk Wars leaves Early Access tomorrow!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/c79bb06b97636a60b3ae5d1f0799f28fd4eb4066.jpg[/img]

[h1]Hello Dieselpunk Builders![/h1]

We are just one day away from the final release! We can’t wait to show you guys the final result of our work so today we're going to talk about not one, not two, but three new features! This will also conclude our list of big changes planned for patch 1.1.0 that will go live once Dieselpunk Wars leaves early access.

Before we start, check out our latest trailer for a sneak peek of the upcoming changes!
[previewyoutube=BWZQzYLd3sw;full][/previewyoutube]

Exciting, isn't it? Now, let's talk about the final three features.

[h2]New Map[/h2]

Your prayers have been answered! We added a new map based on your feedback, perfect for testing out your biggest creations on a large battlefield! The map features wide, open plains, woods, small hills, as well as two small but relatively deep lakes. There are few rocks or cliffs and in general, your vehicles shouldn't be hindered by difficult terrain. This map is built for speed! There are also no structures on the new map - we felt that adding any buildings would be a limitation for any scenarios you would want to create. Instead, you have total freedom to add as many fortifications in the Battle Simulator mode as you like! And if you're not sure how then check out our last update!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/425a04791f1e4c80ddbd3fc876572e822ce0808a.jpg[/img]

[h2]Copy/Paste in Battle Simulator[/h2]

Did you create a really cool vehicle for your Battle Simulator scenario and wish to add more of them? In patch 1.1.0 you can simply press E to create a copy of your currently selected vehicle. All to maximize your efficiency! Play the game how you like it and explore all of the possibilities. 

[h2]The ability to share player-made scenarios via Steam Workshop[/h2]

This is our biggest new feature and one that we were most anxious to reveal! Many of the other features we talked about - the new map, battle simulator improvements, and so on - were made just to make better use of this incredible new functionality!

It works just like sharing your vehicles, by utilizing Steam Workshop. All you need to do is design your own scenario, fill it with vehicles, fortifications, and targets. Once you're satisfied, just share your work with other players so they can give your scenario a try! Remember to mark one of the vehicles as a player vehicle for a more immersive experience. And if you added any custom vehicles to your scenario, make sure to share them on the Steam Workshop too!

We believe that our wonderful community (that means you!) will create many epic and challenging battles and that our Steam Workshop page will soon be filled with interesting challenges. Come up with a challenging battle plan and see how your friends adapt to it!

[h1]We are almost there![/h1]

Let us know what you think about this update. Join our [url=https://discord.gg/wgZA6EA9]Discord server[/url] and stay in touch with our upcoming releases. See you there!

notes.title: New Feature Announced!
notes.content:
[url=https://i.imgur.com/dejdkpJ.jpg][img]https://i.imgur.com/dejdkpJ.jpg[/img][/url]

[h1]Hello, engineers![/h1]

We know you're waiting for more news about the upcoming patch 1.1.0 and so, we prepared a special treat for you: two new features instead of one! We hope you're as excited as we are!

Firstly, something big. We implemented a function that allows the players to add structures in the Battle Simulator mode! Previously, you would have to either make use of pre-existing structures that are already on a map or create an immobile vehicle to act as a structure. You can still do that, of course, but you also have the option to add some of the buildings that you've seen on our maps.

And that isn't all! Adding buildings is fun but what's even cooler is an ability to specify targets in Battle Simulator. And by targets, we mean key objectives that have to be achieved. Additionally, you can designate a vehicle to be a player vehicle by default - meaning that when you start a battle simulation, you will immediately gain control of that vehicle. So you can easily create complex scenarios and play them out. Pretty cool, right?

[url=https://i.imgur.com/5zUqz7M.jpg][img]https://i.imgur.com/5zUqz7M.jpg[/img][/url]

Secondly, a quality of life improvement that many of you have asked for. You now can control rotors with your mouse instead of using a keyboard! It might be a small thing but improving the controls is something we've been doing ever since Dieselpunk Wars was released. After all, we don't want the controls to get in the way of either building or destroying your opponents.

That is all for this update! Did you enjoy it? We have even better features planned for the upcoming patch 1.1.0 so stay tuned! You can share your excitement with us on our Discord server too! We would love to see you there :D

[h1]Best regards,
Image Power Team[/h1]

Our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/952240/announcements/detail/3033707388030052024]competition[/url] has ended and we’ve got the winners!

Congratulations to our community members! We will send you a [b]Dieselpunk Wars key[/b] soon and assign a [b]Skillful Builder role on our Discord server[/b].

Thank you for participating and we encourage you to take a part in our contests in the future. Your skills are amazing and your imagination is impressive. Don’t waste your potential!

[h2]New update![/h2]

We are also happy to inform you that we released patch 1.0.5. Our main focus was improving the Endless Mode which we still weren't quite satisfied with. [b]Check out the changelog below[/b]:

💥 The number of enemies present in the Endless Mode is limited to 5 at a time. If more than five enemies are meant to spawn during a single wave, these enemies will wait until the player destroys one of the opponents. Thanks to this, the player will not be instantly destroyed by a swarm of powerful enemies on higher levels.
💥 It's no longer possible to trigger a double wave spawn by repeatedly pressing the button to start the next wave.
💥 Enemy waves are more consistent. Before, it was possible for more enemies to appear in wave 4 than in wave 5. Now, this shouldn't happen.
💥 We increased the probability of new weapon unlocks after defeating each wave.

notes.title: Dieselpunk Wars nearly finished, backer rewards, and a redesigned tutorial
notes.content:
Greetings! It's been a long time since our last update and we apologize for the prolonged silence. Nevertheless, we prepared an awesome new update to bring you all back to speed!

First of all, we know that you're all waiting for a release date announcement. Dieselpunk Wars has been in production for a long time now and it's almost time we share it with the world. We're very eager to let our players get their hands on our game! As such, we plan to announce the release date in the next update, not too long from now!

This might seem like a cautious approach on our part but it's all for the good of the player. We need to make sure that there are as little bugs as possible for the official release. We've all worked very hard on this game and we don't want any issues to spoil your fun. Last week alone we fixed over [b]130 [/b]bugs! That is an incredibly high number and we're going to keep this pace up until we're ready for launch.

There is another thing we need to discuss in regards to [b]backer rewards[/b] and backer surveys. So far, we haven't received many responses to our surveys and even fewer people answered our emails about their specific custom-made in-game rewards. If you haven't heard from us and need to discuss your rewards, please email us at kontakt@imagepower.pl and we'll answer any questions you may have. Please note that this is only relevant for people with custom-made rewards, such as their own vehicle in the game. If you answered all questions via the survey and didn't need to send us additional files, then all is good and your name is in the game!

Speaking of rewards, take a look at one of the vehicles we created for our backers:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/63a4d47844a0843e85234c166827581a70fae592.jpg[/img]

Finally, let's discuss the tutorial. We've heard the complaints some people had in regards to the tutorial you currently see in Dieselpunk Wars Prologue and we listened! As a result, we completely redesigned the tutorial and changed its format. The new tutorial is split into several different lessons and you can play them out in any order you want. So there's no need to learn about camera controls if you only want to learn more about making an aerodynamic vehicle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/123a2f466c8093b8740c80b1a30d09a741cfe5c0.jpg[/img]

We want to add this new tutorial to Dieselpunk Wars Prologue as soon as possible, alongside dozens of other fixes and improvements. However, we have to prioritize QA above everything else so for now we'll simply continue fixing bugs and polishing our game. Only once it's almost ready for release, we will update the Prologue with a new, fancy tutorial!

As always, a huge THANK YOU for your support over the past few months. You're all amazing and can't wait to share our game with you! This is the final stretch before release and the full version of Dieselpunk Wars will soon be here!

Thanks for reading and keep an eye out for our next update! In the meantime, consider joining our [url=https://discord.gg/EqNvs7T]official Discord channel[/url] to meet with other Dieselpunk enthusiasts!

notes.title: Unleashing creativity within the gaming community
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/e4bea706b1ffd486103d578b7ea26445e3d24757.jpg[/img]


[b]A game doesn’t exist without its players; they are one of the most crucial elements, especially when it comes to titles that are creatively engaging. We’ve designed a game which we want to be intriguing from two perspectives - creative- and gameplay-wise, so that players can boost each other with new ideas and positive energy. [/b]

Our goal was to create a huge community and even though we’re still at the beginning of our journey, we can proudly say that we have already succeeded. However, it’s not only about numbers; we’re mostly focused on having a committed team of players that we can work with and get feedback from. This way we’re creating a bond between us - the creators and them - the players, making the game something we get involved in together, rather than just a digital product we sell. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/f42380cc43afbe683b066781a20d33b58978d94a.jpg[/img]

From the very beginning, [b]Dieselpunk Wars[/b] was focused on giving players the freedom of choice. We started with an idea of a sandbox game, which later evolved and developed additional modes, such as single player campaign. Nonetheless, our main goal was to unleash the inner engineers within players and help them use their imagination to build one-of-a-kind war machines, which will then fight each other in extraordinary battles. 

We love the projects made by our players. Every time they convince us that the path we chose is right and we gave them exactly what they needed to enjoy the game. We are in constant contact with our community, so we’re trying to respond to all of their ideas and needs to make our game better. For example, back in one of the earliest builds you couldn’t place weapons on the bottom of your vehicle. However - one of the users created a war machine that had cannons on top, but it was able to turn itself upside down. This inspired us to add a mounting which now allows to attach bottom artillery and at the same time proves that we created a game without impossible things. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/ae91add6a19adc98105beedd7e64c280f8582d13.png[/img]

Two heads are better than one, they say. That’s why we listen to our players and use their in-game experience in order to improve [b]Dieselpunk Wars[/b]. We’ve been following this rule since the launch of our Kickstarter campaign and even took the cooperation with players to another level. Some of our backers - people interested in the concept of the game who wanted to get involved at the earliest stage of the production - were given a unique opportunity. They received a chance to design a particular in-game module, an entire vehicle or even a map that will later be used for battles. It was our way of expressing gratitude and thanking them for their trust.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/8a09560a884ac0f8ac55f44fc03713af1365b995.jpg[/img]

[b]Dieselpunk Wars[/b] is not only a game. It’s a close community, full of creative and imaginative people, willing to devote their time to building something unusual. Making such a game is a wonderful experience for us, because we know we’re creating something that’s not only enjoyable and entertaining, but also forming a bond between people. We’re not just selling them our product, we’re supporting each other. They help us make a better game and in return we provide them with a product that gives them a lot of fun.

We’re not stopping here! We just kicked off an event called [b]#DieselpunkCommunity[/b]. Every Tuesday we will share your builds and show them to the rest of the Dieselpunk Wars Community. We’d love to see what you have created! Read more about [b]#DieselpunkCommunity[/b] here: [url=http://bit.ly/DieselpunkCommunity]Dieselpunk Community[/url]. Have fun building!

notes.title: What is dieselpunk? Why did we choose this setting?
notes.content:
People tend to imagine alternate realities - probably because we like to ask the “what if” question too much. We’re creating worlds where history changed its course, where peculiar breakthroughs happened, where different decisions were made. The worldbuilding is limited only by our own imagination. It’s also the most appreciated part of fantasy universes and the reason why so many “-punk” worlds exist nowadays. There are multiple ways of creating environments which are significantly distinctive from the reality we all know and every single one of them is extraordinary.

Choosing a proper background for a game is a hard, but important decision to make. It will not only define all of the visible elements, like design, assets or the environment. It will also have a major impact on each of the in-game mechanics and rules that help keep the whole product believable and logical. There must be a reason to set a game in a specific setting - otherwise it won’t be entertaining enough.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/e7bbd5186423092a0a147f1da2ddd300119eb0e1.jpg[/img]

Dieselpunk world is an incredibly interesting vision. It’s a concept of an alternate dimension, where the forties never ended and technology improved way faster. The overall atmosphere remained gloomy and the fear of war was still growing. However, even though it's full of worrying conflicts, the need of progress has led to the development of technology, which gave the society much more possibilities. This makes the people of dieselpunk full of hope for a better tomorrow.  

During the early development of Dieselpunk Wars we were mostly thinking about proper aesthetics. Something that will not only go with the concept of fighting machines but what will also make them more interesting and unique, since the vehicles sent into battles are going to be built by players themselves. Following gaming trends and newest releases we discovered that not many titles follow the idea of a setting, where machinery and creativity join together to form a progressive world. Where past meets future, modern technologies meet dirt, most of the machines are used in wars. Suddenly we realized that we had exactly what we needed. What could be better for a military game than a world dominated by combat vehicles? Vehicles that players can build themselves!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/61692dd97e909bcf4b0379b34baf5ef00090dec7.jpg[/img]

Our main goal was to give players the possibility to create their own designs: land-, air- and water-based. Since the dieselpunk era is way ahead of our world, when it comes to technology, we knew that the potential results of constructions can be really surprising. Not only because of the design itself, but also because of the functionality on the battlefield. No other era uses progress in such an innovative and surprising way. We know that players’ creativity will exceed all of our daring expectations and we cannot wait to see their creations!

Dieselpunk is definitely one of our favourite settings. We love seeing how people’s imagination builds up and materializes in even the wildest visions, which seemed improbable in the beginning. We wanted to provide the best possible environment for this and dieselpunk seemed like a perfect fit. Our greatest hope is that our game will make even more people fell in love with this setting and what is has to offer.

notes.title: Dieselpunk Wars Prologue on steam, UI nearly finished, new main menu

Greetings! We hope that everybody's doing okay. We have an exciting new update for you!

First of all, we have some big and exciting news to share! After a series of internal discussions, we decided to publish a demo version of Dieselpunk Wars early! Our original plan was to make it available on Steam at the same time as the full version of the game. But after reworking the tutorial and retrofitting our user interface, we realized that there is little to no reason to wait any longer.

How can you play the new, updated demo? Well, it's not out just yet - [b]we will release it on the 20th of April[/b]. If you're a backer, your Kickstarter demo should automatically download via Steam. Otherwise, you should head over to a [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1275590/Dieselpunk_Wars_Prologue/]brand new Steam page for Dieselpunk Wars: Prologue[/url]! Yes, that was a link, click it, you know you want to.

What can you expect from Dieselpunk Wars: Prologue? It's the same as our demo but better. The same core features that you enjoyed are still in the game. Our physics engine is still very advanced, able to track every projectile, calculate its trajectory, and even make it ricochet if it impacts armor from the right angle. Vehicles can still be cut in half, set on fire, flooded, or crushed. All that good stuff is there and it's free - with no microtransactions what so ever.

As for improvements - Dieselpunk Wars: Prologue will have a number of bugs fixed, a cleaner UI, and a cooler main menu. Let's talk a bit about them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/78b9a802d0b5f63137b101949aeb9e8e786b32a0.jpg[/img]

Our new UI is already functional and ready for its official reveal! As you can see, we reduced the screen space occupied by the UI by a fair bit. It should be a lot less invasive now. You also have an option to hide unnecessary panels to free up even more space. This should be a lot less confusing for new players and it will hopefully reduce the time you need to learn the controls.

Looking for new parts has never been easier. We added a lot of new categories so you don't need to scroll through an endless list of parts to find the one you need. Additionally, you now have a small panel where you can assign the parts that you want to use. It's less messy this way and it frees up a lot of valuable screen space. There are still some small tweaks that we need to do but we're happy with this new UI and we can't wait to hear your feedback.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/02d9049cdfd84b11dda89e854e6fdfb1ccf15469.jpg[/img]

We also took a look at our main menu. First impressions are very important after all and we didn't feel like the old menu was good enough. It needed more action and a better overall aesthetic. So we changed some things and added a new background full of explosions. You can take a sneak peek of the new menu below:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/2d23f467ed2c95538d42474301400b11fbbc5e52.jpg[/img]

That's everything for now! To summarize: we improved our demo and will release it on the [b]20th of April[/b] for free on a [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1275590/Dieselpunk_Wars_Prologue/]separate Steam page[/url]. Kickstarter backers don't have to swap to a new version but we encourage everybody to do so, since Dieselpunk Wars: Prologue will support Steam achievements and workshop - something our Kickstarter demo can't do.

Thank you for supporting us and staying by our side! We wish everyone to stay safe. Take care and let's meet again when we post another update!

notes.title: Progress report: desert map, UI rework, and new weapons
notes.content:
It's been a while since our last announcement, so here's what we've been up to:

We're making steady progress on Dieselpunk Wars. Most of it is difficult to show, despite how important it is. Dozens of bugs big and small have been fixed and just as many improvements were made. Nevertheless, we want to keep you in the loop - so here are the three most flashy things we did:

Firstly, the desert map you funded (for which we're still very grateful, thank you ♥). It's shaping up to be the most expansive map in Dieselpunk Wars, matched in size only by the infinite ocean of the island map (which isn't really fair). We're hoping that this map will serve the story of the campaign mode well, while also giving the players plenty of space where they can engineer their own battles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/f35e037d67e4731b79c4b750f4d338c2d2d6c85e.jpg[/img]

As you can see on the screenshot above, our desert isn't just a flat patch of sand. That would be far too boring. Instead, we have a small canyon, a river with some fertile land near it, and something special that we don't want to spoil just yet. And of course sand, loads of rocks and sand. Turns out, you need a lot of sand to make a desert, who knew?

Once the terrain is fully completed, we're going to add story missions for the campaign mode to it and work on post-processing, fog, and similar effects. Fear not, a scenario for this map is already done, so adding everything in shouldn't take too long!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/e7bbd5186423092a0a147f1da2ddd300119eb0e1.jpg[/img]

Beyond this, we're still overhauling the UI. We're not quite yet ready to show it to you but we can tell you a bit about it! The build mode is what we tackled first since it needed improvements the most. Our new idea for the UI is a modular design - with the player controlling just how much information they want to see. This allows us to hide unnecessary windows until the player actually needs them for something. We freed up a ton of screen space just with this change.

This isn't everything of course! We also changed our approach to how parts are displayed. The old window will be replaced with a small, compact bar, showing only a few parts at a time. The player will be able to configure this bar by choosing what parts they want easy access to. This process is also streamlined, with many new categories for parts and more ways to sort and filter them.

Finally, we're still adding new and exciting weapons to the existing arsenal of Dieselpunk Wars! The most recent addition are two massive miniguns that will tear enemies to shreds! Due to their high rate of fire and large caliber, we had to balance them out somehow. We decided to use the heat mechanic. Now a minigun generates heat with every bullet fired, forcing a player to invest in efficient heat disposal if they want to use those fearsome weapons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34146173/d802416203b44647f185ca9df5089815f97a5465.jpg[/img]

That is all for today, thanks for reading! And in light of the recent global events, our entire team wishes everyone to be in good health. Stay at home if you can and relax while playing some fun games. Stay safe and keep an eye out for the next update!

notes.title: Open world and missions
notes.content:
Hi, the world to exploration  consists of 3 large islands and a large number of smaller ones with different biomes.
In addition to the grassy island, it will be a desert one with canyon, icy one, swamps, volcanic and something special under water
There will be also cities, industry, ports, airport and fortified bases. Almost all of these structures can be destroyed by means of weapons or ramming

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/4feef87267d971a03641a6fa363ee939d2c0116b.jpg[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/43df1112edc41b69c5235d5cd80e53cf2220fc9d.jpg[/img]

In main mode to unlock all elements and increase limit as large you can build, you must carry out the missions located around the world and collect screws (for decorative elements).
A mission is chosen by drive to question mark, their goal may be to destroy enemy vehicles or buildings, win a race, transport something or survive
For these activities and for destruction of aggressive vehicles or buildings, you also get an experience point to unlock skills

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/903e9e8dd1030a3ba3e3b365b631d8c5291631e5.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Missions, skill tree, level progression
notes.content:
Main game goal will be increasing potential to build larger and more advanced vehicles and developing the captain's abilities in similar way like in RPG games.
Reward for completing a missions is experience points, unlocking new parts and increase strength limit, for which you can build a vehicle. Strength of vehicle is sum of strength of its elements.

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/b84332d6c012da81b128165aeb5ba4f94b0d0227.jpg][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/b40eb3409c8398546ba3075dcc23da66555b8b51.jpg[/img][/url]

In addition to passive skills that increase statistics, you can also choose 4 active skills, activated with keys, with cooldown.
Thanks to them you can make a small repair during the mission (because you can't rebuild vehicle during mission), temporarily increase the firepower or speed, etc. There is also a skill that allows you to switch weapons to be controlled by AI.
[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/e35d12af5b7ce1e7b1d719603c129fe487b8470a.jpg][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/8bd490d4b4b50c9d1fbf9092ccce43a3689cf9a7.jpg[/img][/url]

notes.title: Water vehicles
notes.content:
Hello, this part is about making stable, not sinking and fast water constructions. At first vehicle need displacement to stay above water surface, hull blocks have buoyancy dependent  to its material, wood have best but is most fragile. Others element have any buoyancy so must be enough and well placement hull blocks.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/d2923cdae00e9dce2163dd5712e96d4e1eff14c5.jpg[/img]

To help find the right balance, you can turn on indicators in corner of screen

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/4159b3fbedd78e2d7fd29b8b6b416ec702e627c8.jpg[/img]

When the ship rolls over or when hull blocks take damages they will start to take in water, vehicle lose its displacement and going to sink, but pump and repair blocks can hold back this

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/2a448e01037b61e1de87bb834ee2edc64d1ff750.jpg[/img]

To move and control vehicle in water you need some kind of propulsion like screw, paddle wheel or sail and a steer. Also using more slopes in hull construction make ship faster without needed to add more engines and propulsions.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34146173/228cf9f153debeecec7e332584cfa554f2f8e949.jpg[/img]
